1. The present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) which was treated as claim petition under sections 166(4) of 'Motor Vehicle Act, 1988' on behalf of the petitioner Ashwani was filed by the Investigating A g e n c y i n r e s p e c t o f t h e i n j u r i e s s u s t a i n e d b y t h e p e t i t i o n e r i n a ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 1 of 25 Pages motor vehicular accident that occurred within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal.
2. In connection with the accident, FIR no. 939/2022, under sections 279/337 IPC, was registered at PS Seemapuri, Delhi on 17.12.2022 on the statement of the petitioner Ashwani.

As per FIR, on 16.12.2022 at about 10:30 p.m., the petitioner on his motorcycle bearing no. DL1SR-7617 was on his way back home after taking off from his job as Delivery Boy under Amazon Company and when he reached Apsara Border Flyover, leading towards Dilshad Garden, Seemapuri, Delhi, just before the Toll Tax Booth, a truck bearing registration number DL1L-AG-4518 (hereinafter, "offending vehicle") being driven by its driver at a high speed, rashly and negligently, came and hit him from Dar-Ashwani vs Nikka Ram on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39065744/
1 behind.
After the collision, the petitioner fell down on the road along with his motorcycle and received injuries on his chest and waist.
The driver stopped and seeing the injured lying down, fled from there with his truck.

Someone called police at phone number 112 and the injured/ petitioner was taken to GTB Hospital, Delhi, where he was medically attended vide MLC no. E/9902/29/22.
3.

During investigation, it was found out that, at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was being driven by the respondent no.1 Nikka Ram, owned by respondent no.2 Sanjeev Kumar and insured by respondent no.3/ Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.

After completion of the investigation,
charge-sheet for offences under sections 279/337 IPC was filed before the concerned court against ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 2 of 25 Pages the respondent no.1 and the present DAR against the respondents was filed before this Tribunal.
4. In response to the DAR, all the three respondents appeared before this Tribunal and subsequently filed their written-statements.

5. In the joint written-statement filed on behalf of respondents no.1 and 2, it is stated that the alleged offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case and no accident as alleged ever occurred or caused by the act of rash and negligent driving of the vehicle of the answering respondents.
It is stated that the petitioner in collusion with the police got the present DAR filed in order to extort money from the answering respondents.

It is stated that the vehicle of respondents was duly insured with the respondent no.3/ insurance company for the period from 03.03.2022 to 02.03.2023 and the respondent no.1 was having a driving licence bearing no. HP-2319960023968 valid upto 02.07.2027 and hence, liability, if any, the insurance company shall be liable for the same.

6. The respondent no.3/ insurance company in its written-statement has inter-alia stated that the driving licence no. HP-2319960023968 issued to the driver/ respondent no.1 was for driving the LMV NT only but in the present case, he was driving the Tata Truck LPT, which was a Transport/
Commercial/ Goods Carriage Vehicle and therefore, for violating the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the answering respondent/ insurance company is entitled for recovery rights.

Upon pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 21.11.2023, following issues were framed:
1.

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 16.12.2022 at about 10:30 p.m. on the road of Apsara Flyover, going towards Dilshad Garden,
within the jurisdiction of PS Seemapuri, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no. DL1LAG-4518, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?

(OPP) 
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP)

Ld.
Court Commissioner submitted their report containing the following depositions:

( a) PW1 Ashwani Kumar, the injured/ petitioner, testified on the strength of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A regarding the manner of accident, injuries sustained, treatment taken and losses suffered as a result of the accident and relied upon the documents Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/7.
(b) PW2 Dr. Anurag Anand, Senior Resident, Department of Orthopaedics, GTB Hospital, Delhi produced the hospital record with respect to issuance of permanent disability certificate no.891/33/09/2024, dated 13.09.2024 to the petitioner and proved the said permanent disability certificate along with assessment ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 4 of 25 Pages sheet as Ex.PW2/1 (colly), as per which the petitioner was found to have suffered 23% permanent disability in relation to right shoulder/ upper limb.
9. As per the report of the Court Commissioner, petitioner has concluded his evidence but the respondents including the insurance company did not lead any evidence.
At the stage of final arguments also, learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that as per instructions, no evidence is to be led.

Accordingly, evidence of respondents was closed vide order dated 08.07.2025.
10.
I have heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsels for the parties and also perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1

Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the accident occurred on 16.12.2022 at about 10:30 p.m. on the road of Apsara Flyover going towards Dilshad Garden, within the jurisdiction of PS Seemapuri, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing no.
DL1LAG-4518, being driven by respondent no.1/ driver? (OPP)
11.
It is settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted b y t h e C l a i m s T r i b u n a l .

H o w e v e r , t h a t d o e s n o t ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 5 of 25 Pages mean that a Tribunal that has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic Dar-Ashwani vs Nikka Ram on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39065744/
3 principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation, which is still based on a tortious liability.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co.
Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012; Bimla Devi &
Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530; Parmeshwari v.
Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096; Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018,
Law Suit (SC) 303; & Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.
12.

sentences.text: In the case in hand, the evidence adduced by the petitioner who received injuries in the accident is of much importance.

The PW1 (petitioner) deposed by way of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A that on 16.12.2022 at around 10:30 p.m., when he was coming back from work as Amazon Delivery Executive, he was driving a motorcycle no. DL1SR-7617 on the correct side of the road and was going towards Dilshad Garden, however, near Apsara Border Flyover when he reached near the Toll Tax Booth, the offending vehicle bearing no. DL1AG-4518 being driven at a high speed, rashly and negligently, came towards him from behind and hit him with great force, as a result, he along with his motorcycle fell down on road and received injuries on his chest and abdomen and driver/
respondent no.1 upon looking him on the ground ran away in haste.

PW1 deposed that he ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 6 of 25 Pages was taken to GTB Hospital, where his MLC no. E/9902/29/22 was prepared and on 17.12.2022, regarding the accident, a criminal case vide FIR no. 939/2022, under section 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Seemapuri.

In support of his deposition, the petitioner PW1 relied upon the following documents:
(i) DAR filed by the IO which is already annexed in the court file and sane is hereby exhibited as Ex.PW1/1 (colly).
(Objected to by the learned counsel for R3 as the said DAR cannot be exhibited in his manner neither the judicial file of the case nor DAR of the case is in original with present Ld. LC).
(ii) Original medical bills, amounting to Rs.5,923/ of the petitioner is Ex.PW1/2 (colly.-5 sheets).

(iii) Copy of treatment record of the petitioner is Ex.PW1/3 (colly.-2 sheets) (OSR)
(Objected to by the counsel for R3 for not filing the original treatment record).

(iv) Cop of educational documents are Ex.PW1/4 (colly.-3 sheets) (OSR).
(v) Copy of Aadhaar Card and PAN Card of the injured is Ex.PW1/5 (colly.-2 sheet)
(OSR).

(vi) Copy of Driving License is Ex.PW1/6 (OSR).
(vii) Bank Account Statement is Ex.PW1/7 (colly.-23 sheets).

I left my office at about 10 p.m.

The offending vehicle had hit me from behind (Vol.

sentences.text: It is correct that in my affidavit the offending vehicle is written as bus (Vol. It is a typographical mistake).
The accident took place before Toll Tax Booth.
It is wrong to suggest that the petition have been filed in connivance with ulterior motive and to harass the respondents or that to extort the money.
It is wrong to suggest that no accident took place by the offending vehicle.
It is wrong to suggest that the respondent/ driver and owner have been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is wrong to suggest that no accident caused by the respondent no.1."

Further, with respect to the manner of accident, in the cross-examination conducted by learned counsel for respondent no.3/ insurance company, PW1 stated that, "I was hit by the offending vehicle coming from behind and hit me on my right and I and my motorcycle fell on the left side."
Rest of the cross-examination is on other aspects.

Thus, in the entire cross- examination of the petitioner (PW1), this Tribunal finds nothing that may demolish or discredit his testimony with respect to the mode and manner of the accident as deposed by him regarding rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1 and thereby causing his accident.

14. The version of the petitioner qua occurrence of the accident due to rash/ negligent driving of respondent no.1 is also found corroborated and supported by the DAR filed by the Investigating Officer, comprising of FIR, Site Plan, Mechanical Inspection Reports and Seizure Memos of both the vehicles involved in the accident, notice under section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, MLC of the injured/ petitioner and charge-sheet.
______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 8 of 25 Pages 15.
It is evident that the FIR was registered after few hours of the accident only and registration number of the offending vehicle is found clearly mentioned in the FIR.
Further, the Mechanical Inspection Reports of both the vehicles involved in the accident show the accidental damages which also support the case of the petitioner.

16. Also, it is not disputed that the respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of charge-sheet support the version of petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
17.
Moreover, there is no challenge from the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle to the version of the petitioner.

The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the petitioner regarding the mode and manner of the Dar-Ashwani vs Nikka Ram on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39065744/
5 accident but he preferred not to enter the witness box during the course of inquiry nor challenged the testimony of the petitioner with respect to the mode and manner of the accident by cross-examining the petitioner.
Even the insurance company did not make any effort to summon the respondent no.1 in the witness box to prove negligence on the part of the petitioner, if any, in the happening of the accident.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. sentences.text: The MLC of the petitioner, prepared at GTB Hospital, Delhi, which is part of the DAR, clearly shows the history of RTA.
Further, the treatment record Ex.PW1/3 (colly) shows that the petitioner sustained 'closed fracture lateral right clavicle' and thus, he received grievous injury.

19. In view of the above, it is held that petitioner has been able to establish on the basis of the preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in the present motor vehicular accident, which was caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.
Issue no.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of the petitioner.
ISSUE NO.2
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 20. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, enjoins the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on large peripheral field.
A man is not compensated f o r t h e p h y s i c a l i n j u r y t h a t h e m i g h t

__________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 10 of 25 Pages have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place, rather he is compensated for the loss, which he suffered as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 10 SCC 34; Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v.
K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].

PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 23.
The petitioner/ injured (PW1) has placed on record the medical bills for a total sum of Rs.5,923/- with respect to his treatment and proved the same as Ex.PW1/2 (colly).
Said bills are in original and are found in order and appears to have not been challenged on any serious count.
Hence, petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.5,923/- under this head.

Loss of Earning During Treatment 2 4 . T h e t r e a t m e n t r e c o r d E x . P W 1 / 3 ( c o l l y ) s h o w s t h a t i m m e d i a t e l y a f t e r ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 11 of 25 Pages the accident which occurred on 16.12.2022, the petitioner was taken to GTB Hospital, where he was diagnosed to have suffered closed fracture of lateral 1/3rd of right clavicle.
The record shows that the petitioner made several visits to the hospital for his treatment.

Though it appears that complete medical treatment documents have not been placed on record, however, considering the nature of injury, it may be safely assumed that the petitioner could not have been in a position to do any work at least for two months from the date of accident.
Hence, petitioner is entitled to be compensated for the loss of income of two months during treatment.

25. The petitioner (PW1) has deposed that he was earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
In her cross-examination has stated that he was working at the MM Logistics Company as a Delivery Boy under Amazon at A-26, Site-4, near Sahibabad.
Further, he stated in cross-examination that he has placed on record the salary slips and bank statements.
However, on perusal of record, it is found that no salary slips have been placed on record and only bank statement has been filed, which has been proved as Ex.PW1/7 (colly).

Though the bank statement reflect that every month some amount is being credited into his account through NEFT from 'M &
ML Logistics Solution' but said amount varies every month i.e. Rs.13,167/- in July 2022; Rs.15,236/-
in August 2022; Rs.14,107/- in September 2022; Rs.11,286/- in October 2022; Rs.18,622/- in November 2022 and Rs.13,761/- in December 2022.

The aforesaid bank statement corroborates the version of the petitioner that he was employed with 'M & ML Logistics Solution' from which he was g e t t i n g  
s a l a r y  
e v e r y  
m o n t h .

Since, the salary slips showing the exact salary of the petitioner have not been placed on record and the amount that he was getting from his employer varies every month as per bank the statement, it would be in the interest of justice, if median of the salary received so from July-2022 to December-2022 is taken as his monthly salary, which comes to Rs.14,363/- [(13,167+15,236+14,107+11,286+ 18,622 +13,761)/6].
Thus, the income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.14,363/- per month.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.28,726/- (14,363x2) is granted to the petitioner on account of loss of two months' income during treatment.

26.

As per disability certificate bearing no. 891/33/9/2024, dated 13.0.9.2024, issued by the Medical Board of GTB Hospital, which has been proved on record by PW2 (doctor) as Ex.PW2/1, the petitioner was assessed to have suffered 23% permanent disability in relation to his right shoulder.

27. The disablement and loss of earning capacity are two different aspects and not substitute for each other and the loss of income has to be seen considering the profession in which the petitioner was engaged at the time of the accident.
28. In cross-examination, the doctor (PW2) stated that he has brought two original x-ray films of AP view and axial view of right shoulder joint of the petitioner.
As per AP view x-ray dated 05.08.2024 and axial view x-ray dated 22.08.2024, there is malunited right lateral end clavicle fracture.

Nikka Ram & Ors. 13 of 25 Pages petitioner will be able to drive motorcycle with said disability or not, the doctor (PW2) replied that the petitioner might have difficulty in driving motorcycle as per assessment sheet.

29. Evidently, the petitioner was a Delivery Boy under Amazon and his job was to deliver the goods on motorcycle to the customers, but as clarified by the doctor (PW2), due to the aforementioned 23% permanent disability in his right shoulder, the petitioner would face difficulty in driving the motorcycle, which would mean that his work would be affected to a considerable extent and due to having difficulty driving the motorcycle, he would not be able to resume his work of delivering orders on the motorcycle as a Delivery Boy.

Hence, this Tribunal is of the opinion that considering effect of the permanent disability on the nature of the job the petitioner was engaged in prior to the accident, functional disability in relation to the whole body of the petitioner may be considered to be 20% for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of his future income.
30. Further, the law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges 32.
Though the petitioner has not led any specific evidence in respect of the money spent by him towards special diet, transport expenses and attendant charges.
As per treatment record, the petitioner was diagnosed to have sustained "closed fracture lateral right clavicle".
His treatment continued in the OPD of GTB Hospital, Delhi.
As per treatment record, he also consulted at Ganesh Ortho Trauma & Medical Center, Krishna Nagar, Delhi.

Considering the nature of the injury and the OPD visits made by the petitioner for his treatment, as per treatment record, it can be safely inferred that the petitioner had to spend a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the ______________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 180/23; Ashwani v. Nikka Ram & Ors. 15 of 25 Pages purpose of early recovery as well as visiting the hospital/ doctor during further treatment.
Accordingly, the petitioner is awarded a total sum of Rs.50,000/- for special diet and conveyance charges.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Pain & Sufferings 33.

Considering the nature of injury and period of treatment, petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering that he had to suffer during treatment of the injuries received in the accident.
Loss of Amenities 34.

It is evident that even after completion of the treatment, the petitioner has suffered 23%
permanent disability in relation to his right shoulder which has been assessed by this Tribunal as 20% functional disability of his whole body.

It cannot be ignored that with the aforementioned permanent disability, the petitioner is bound to face difficulties to a certain extent throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
Hence, a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

ISSUE NO.3 (INTEREST)
36.
The petitioner shall also be entitled for interest @ 6% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the DAR till realization.
LIABILITY 37.

The insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and, in the present case, learned counsel for the insurance company has contended that the driver/
